units.source_text: 人到中年，面对棋盘自然而然地变得轻灵飘洒，

en.t: When people reach middle age, they naturally become lighter and more graceful before the go board,

units.source_text: 如今不重视礼节，也许正由于这一点，年轻棋手时而扭动身体，时而露出怪样。

en.t: and perhaps because etiquette is no longer valued these days, young players sometimes twist their bodies or show odd expressions.

units.source_text: 我每次看到这种模样，便产生一种异样的感觉。

en.t: Whenever I see such behavior, I feel a strange uneasiness.

units.source_text: 有一回，日本棋院举行升段赛，一位年轻四段一边对弈，

en.t: Once, during a promotion tournament at the Nihon Ki-in, a young fourth-dan player was playing a game,

units.source_text: 一边利用对手还没落子的间隙，把一本文艺同人杂志展放在膝上，读起小说来。

en.t: and during the intervals before his opponent made a move, he spread a literary coterie magazine on his knees and began reading a novel.

units.source_text: 对手一落棋，他就抬头思考，而后自己下了一着。

en.t: As soon as his opponent placed a stone, he would raise his head, think, and then make his own move.

units.source_text: 轮到对手思考，他又佯装不知，把视线落在同人杂志上。

en.t: When it was his opponent's turn to think, he would again pretend not to notice and lower his gaze to the magazine.

units.source_text: 简直是高傲无礼，差点触怒了对手。

en.t: It was utterly arrogant and rude, and it nearly provoked his opponent to anger.

units.source_text: 后来我听说，这位四段不久就疯了。

en.t: Later I heard that this fourth-dan player went mad before long.

units.source_text: 恐怕是对手在思考时他那病弱的神经无法忍受吧。

en.t: Probably his frail nerves could not endure the time when his opponent was thinking.
